title: Why Is English Spelling So Weird?
subtitle: 英文拼字為什麼這麼怪？knight 的 k、debt 的 b 從哪裡來
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈English orthography〉〈Great Vowel Shift〉〈William Caxton〉〈Phonological history of English consonant clusters〉核對，2026-10-22

sources.title: Wikipedia: Phonological history of English consonant clusters

beginner.title: Silent Letters and Lost Sounds
paras: Why does “knight” have a “k”? Why is there a “b” in “debt”? Why don’t “tough” and “dough” rhyme? If English spelling makes you angry, you are not alone. Even native speakers find it hard. But there are reasons for these strange spellings, and they come from history. Some people have tried to make English spelling simpler, but most of their plans failed. In the United States, Noah Webster pushed for simpler spellings, so Americans write “flavor” instead of the British “flavour”.
為什麼 knight 有個 k？為什麼 debt 裡有個 b？為什麼 tough 和 dough 不押韻？如果英文拼字讓你很生氣，你並不孤單，連母語人士都覺得很難。不過，這些奇怪的拼法都有原因，而且來自歷史。有些人試過讓英文拼字更簡單，但大多數的計畫都失敗了。在美國，諾亞．韋伯斯特推動比較簡單的拼法，所以美國人寫 flavor，而不是英式的 flavour。

First, many spellings show old sounds. Long ago, people really said the “k” in “knight” and “knee”. Later, the “k” sound disappeared, but the spelling stayed. Between about 1400 and 1700, the long vowels of English also changed a lot. This is called the Great Vowel Shift.
首先，很多拼法保留的是古老的發音。很久以前，人們真的會把 knight 和 knee 裡的 k 唸出來。後來 k 的音消失了，拼法卻留了下來。大約在 1400 到 1700 年間，英文的長母音也有很大的改變，這叫作「母音大推移」。

Second, printing played a part. In 1476, William Caxton brought the first printing press to England. Some printers knew other languages well. The word “ghost” was once spelled “gost”, but a Flemish spelling with “gh” was used by mistake, and people accepted it.
第二，印刷也有影響。1476 年，威廉．卡克斯頓把第一台印刷機帶進英格蘭。有些印刷工人很熟悉其他語言。ghost 這個字以前拼作 gost，但一種帶有 gh 的法蘭德斯拼法被誤用，後來大家也就接受了。

Third, some scholars added letters on purpose. They wanted English words to look like Latin. “Debt” was once spelled “dette”, but they added a “b” because of the Latin word “debitum”. Nobody ever said the “b”.
第三，有些學者故意加了字母。他們希望英文字看起來像拉丁文。debt 以前拼作 dette，但因為拉丁文的 debitum，他們加了一個 b。從來沒有人唸過這個 b。

So English spelling is like a museum. It keeps old sounds, old mistakes and old ideas. This can help you, too. When you see a strange spelling, ask: “What story is this word telling me?” It may help you remember it.
所以，英文拼字就像一座博物館，保存了古老的發音、過去的錯誤和舊時的觀念。這對你也有幫助。看到奇怪的拼法時，問問自己：「這個字在告訴我什麼故事？」這可能會幫你記住它。

intermediate.title: Why Is English Spelling So Weird?
paras: Tough, dough, through, cough: four words, one spelling pattern, four different pronunciations. English spelling is famously unpredictable, even for educated native speakers. Attempts to reform it have mostly failed. But its strangeness is not random. Almost every odd spelling is a clue to something that happened in the history of the language. One partial exception is Noah Webster, who promoted simpler spellings in the United States, such as “flavor” for British “flavour” and “fiber” for “fibre”.
tough、dough、through、cough：四個字，同一種拼字模式，四種不同的發音。英文拼字出了名地難以預測，連受過教育的母語人士也一樣。改革拼字的嘗試大多失敗了。但它的怪異並不是隨機的。幾乎每個奇怪的拼法，都是語言史上發生過某件事的線索。一個部分的例外是諾亞．韋伯斯特，他在美國推廣比較簡化的拼法，例如用 flavor 取代英式的 flavour，用 fiber 取代 fibre。

One major reason is that pronunciation kept changing after spelling began to settle down. Between roughly 1400 and 1700, English went through the Great Vowel Shift, a series of changes in which every long vowel altered. A word like “bite” once had a vowel closer to the one in modern “beat”. Some consonants also fell silent: in Middle English, the “k” in “knight” and “knot” was pronounced, which is why German still says the “k” in its word for knee, Knie.
一個主要原因是，拼法開始固定下來之後，發音卻還在持續改變。大約在 1400 到 1700 年間，英文經歷了「母音大推移」——一連串改變，所有長母音都變了。像 bite 這樣的字，母音曾經比較接近現代 beat 的母音。有些子音也變得不發音了：在中古英文裡，knight 和 knot 裡的 k 是要唸出來的，這也是為什麼德文表示膝蓋的字 Knie，至今仍然唸出 k。

Printing also left its mark. William Caxton is thought to have introduced the printing press to England in 1476. Many early compositors who set the type were multilingual and occasionally used spelling patterns from other languages. The word “ghost”, spelled “gost” in Middle English, gained its silent “h” from a Flemish pattern that happened to be accepted.
印刷也留下了痕跡。一般認為，威廉．卡克斯頓在 1476 年把印刷機引進英格蘭。許多早期負責排字的工人會說多種語言，偶爾會用上其他語言的拼字模式。中古英文拼作 gost 的 ghost，就是因為一個剛好被接受的法蘭德斯拼法，才多了不發音的 h。

Some silent letters were added deliberately. Scholars who admired Latin altered the spelling of certain words to show their supposed origins. “Debt”, originally “dette”, gained a “b” to link it to Latin debitum, and “doubt” received a similar treatment. The “s” in “island” was added to connect it with Latin insula, even though the word actually comes from Old English. Sometimes there was no good reason at all: the “p” in “ptarmigan”, the name of a bird, was added to make a Gaelic word look Greek.

有些不發音的字母是故意加上去的。崇拜拉丁文的學者，修改了某些字的拼法，好顯示它們被認為的來源。debt 原本拼作 dette，為了連結拉丁文 debitum 而多了個 b，doubt 也受到類似的處理。island 裡的 s，是為了和拉丁文 insula 扯上關係而加上的，儘管這個字其實來自古英文。有時甚至毫無道理可言：鳥名 ptarmigan（雷鳥）裡的 p，是為了讓一個蓋爾語的字看起來像希臘文而加上的。

Seen this way, English spelling is less a set of rules than a historical record. That record can actually help learners. Noticing that “knee” and “knight” share a lost sound, or that “debt” is related to “debit”, turns random memorisation into a story. Spelling, in other words, is a map of where the language has been.
從這個角度來看，英文拼字與其說是一套規則，不如說是一份歷史紀錄。這份紀錄其實能幫助學習者。注意到 knee 和 knight 共有一個消失的音，或 debt 和 debit 有關，就能把死記硬背變成一個故事。換句話說，拼字是一張地圖，記錄著這個語言走過的路。

advanced.title: A Map of Where the Language Has Been
paras: English spelling has a reputation for chaos. The letter sequence “ough” alone is pronounced differently in tough, though, through and cough, and its unpredictability defeats even educated native speakers. Reformers have tried for centuries to regularise it, mostly without success. Yet the system is less arbitrary than it first appears. Its irregularities are largely the residue of identifiable historical processes: sound changes that spelling never caught up with, the habits of early printers, and the ambitions of scholars who wanted English to look more classical.
英文拼字素有混亂之名。光是 ough 這串字母，在 tough、though、through 和 cough 裡的發音就各不相同，它的不可預測性連受過教育的母語人士都招架不住。改革者幾個世紀以來一直試圖讓它規律化，大多徒勞無功。然而，這套系統並不像乍看那麼任意。它的不規則，大多是可辨識的歷史過程留下的殘跡：拼字始終沒追上的語音變化、早期印刷工人的習慣，以及想讓英文看起來更古典的學者們的雄心。

The most important of these processes is the Great Vowel Shift, a series of pronunciation changes that took place primarily between 1400 and 1700. During this period, every long vowel of Middle English altered; the vowel of “bite”, for instance, moved from a sound close to that of modern “beat” to the diphthong heard today. Because the standardisation of spelling had begun in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, written forms were increasingly fixed just as spoken forms were shifting. Consonants were affected too. The initial cluster in “knight” and “knot” was once fully pronounced; most dialects reduced it to a simple /n/ relatively recently, while German cognates such as Knie still retain the /k/.

這些過程中最重要的，是母音大推移——主要發生在 1400 到 1700 年間的一連串發音變化。在這段期間，中古英文的每一個長母音都改變了；例如 bite 的母音，就從接近現代 beat 的音，移到今天聽到的雙母音。由於拼字的標準化在十五、十六世紀就已開始，書面形式逐漸固定的同時，口語形式卻正在移動。子音也受到影響。knight 和 knot 開頭的子音群，過去是完整唸出來的；多數方言是在相對晚近才把它簡化成單純的 /n/，而德文的同源字如 Knie 至今仍保留 /k/。

Technology added another layer. William Caxton is thought to have introduced the printing press to England in 1476, and printing accelerated the fixing of spellings. Early compositors were often multilingual and occasionally imported conventions from other languages; the Middle English “gost”, for example, acquired its silent “h” from a Flemish spelling pattern that happened to stick. Caxton himself was acutely aware of the instability of the language he was printing. In the prologue to his Eneydos, he recalled a northern merchant who asked a Kentish woman for “egges” and was told she spoke no French, because in her dialect the word was “eyren”.

技術又加上了另一層。一般認為，威廉．卡克斯頓在 1476 年把印刷機引進英格蘭，而印刷加速了拼法的固定。早期的排字工人往往會說多種語言，偶爾會引進其他語言的慣例；例如中古英文的 gost，就是從一個碰巧留存下來的法蘭德斯拼字模式，多了一個不發音的 h。卡克斯頓本人非常清楚他所印刷的語言有多不穩定。在《伊尼依多斯》的序言中，他回憶一位北方商人向一位肯特郡婦人要買 egges，卻被告知她不會說法語，因為在她的方言裡，這個字是 eyren。

A final layer was deliberate. Scholars in the Renaissance and after sometimes inserted silent letters to display a word’s classical ancestry. The “b” in “debt” (earlier “dette”) and “doubt” and the “p” in “receipt” were added to evoke Latin, though never pronounced. Some insertions rested on mistaken etymologies: the “s” in “island” was meant to link the word to Latin insula, whereas its true origin is the Old English īġland. Ironically, these efforts to make spelling more learned made it less phonetic.

最後一層是刻意造成的。文藝復興時期及之後的學者，有時會插入不發音的字母，以展示一個字的古典血統。debt（早期拼作 dette）和 doubt 裡的 b，以及 receipt 裡的 p，都是為了喚起拉丁文的聯想而加上的，卻從來不發音。有些插入是建立在錯誤的詞源上：island 裡的 s 本來是要把這個字和拉丁文 insula 連在一起，但它真正的來源是古英文 īġland。諷刺的是，這些讓拼字更有學問的努力，反而讓它更不符合發音。

For learners, this history offers more than trivia. Treating English spelling as a historical record rather than a list of exceptions can make it easier to master. Recognising that “knee” and “knight” preserve a vanished sound, or that “debt” is related to “debit”, transforms arbitrary memorisation into meaningful pattern. Caxton’s own lament remains apt: it is hard to please every man “by cause of dyversite and chaunge of langage”. Spelling is, in the end, a map of where the language has been.
對學習者來說，這段歷史不只是冷知識。把英文拼字當成一份歷史紀錄，而不是一張例外清單，能讓它更容易掌握。認出 knee 和 knight 保存了一個消失的音，或 debt 和 debit 有關，就能把任意的死記轉化成有意義的規律。卡克斯頓自己的感嘆至今依然貼切：因為語言的多樣與變化，要讓每個人滿意實在很難。說到底，拼字就是一張地圖，記錄著語言走過的路。

quote.text: Loo what sholde a man in thyse dayes now wryte, egges or eyren? Certaynly it is harde to playse every man by cause of dyversite and chaunge of langage.
quote.author: William Caxton
quote.work: Prologue to Eneydos (1490), spelling lightly normalised; as quoted in the Wikipedia article “William Caxton”

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How history explains many strange English spellings.
How to spell every English word correctly.
Why the printing press was invented in 1476.
Why Americans write “flavour” with a “u”.
beginner.evidence: But there are reasons for these strange spellings, and they come from history.
beginner.why: 全文：奇怪的拼字來自歷史（舊發音、印刷、學者加字母）。
traps: 捏造：文中沒提供拼字規則。
以偏概全：印刷只是原因之一。
正反顛倒：美式拼法是 flavor。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “people accepted it” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: The old spelling “gost”.
The first printing press in England.
The Flemish spelling of “ghost” with “gh”.
The long vowels of English.
beginner.evidence: a Flemish spelling with “gh” was used by mistake
beginner.why: 前半句：法蘭德斯式的 gh 拼法被誤用，大家就接受了。
traps: 正反顛倒：gost 是被取代的舊拼法。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：印刷機是被引進，不是被接受的拼法。
時序錯置：母音是第二段的內容。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: People used to say the “b” in “debt”.
“Debt” was once spelled “dette”.
The “k” in “knight” was always silent.
The Great Vowel Shift happened after 1900.
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 Nobody ever said the “b”。
正反顛倒：以前 k 是會發音的。
數字錯位：大約 1400 到 1700 年。

beginner.q: How does the writer suggest strange spellings can help learners?
options: They help learners speak with a British accent.
They show that English has no rules at all.
They make reading English much faster.
Their stories can help learners remember the words.
beginner.evidence: It may help you remember it.
beginner.why: 最後一段：拼字背後的故事有助記憶。
traps: 捏造：文中沒談口音。
過度推論：作者說它們有原因，不是沒規則。
捏造：文中沒談閱讀速度。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: English spelling was designed to be difficult on purpose.
English spelling is odd because it records the language’s history.
Noah Webster created all of today’s English spellings.
German and English are spelled in exactly the same way.
intermediate.evidence: Seen this way, English spelling is less a set of rules than a historical record.
traps: 以偏概全：只有少數字母是學者刻意加的。
以偏概全：Webster 只影響了美式拼法。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：德文只是用來證明 k 曾經發音。

intermediate.q: What does “compositors” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
options: Speakers who lost the “k” sound.
Scholars who studied Latin words.
Writers who composed poems in English.
People who set the type for printing.
intermediate.evidence: Many early compositors who set the type were multilingual
intermediate.why: 後面的關係子句說明：負責排字的人。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：k 不發音是第二段的現象。
張冠李戴：學者是第四段的人。
字面誤讀：compose 也有作曲、寫作之意，但這裡是排版。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The “s” in “island” was added to link it with Latin insula.
“Island” actually comes from Latin.
The “p” in “ptarmigan” was added to make a word look Latin.
Caxton brought the printing press to England in 1700.
intermediate.evidence: The “s” in “island” was added to connect it with Latin insula
traps: 正反顛倒：它其實來自古英語。
張冠李戴：是讓蓋爾語的字看起來像希臘文。
數字錯位：1476 年。

intermediate.q: Why does the author mention that German still says the “k” in Knie?
options: To show that German spelling is also very strange.
To prove that English came from German spelling rules.
To show that the “k” in “knee” was once pronounced.
To explain why “knee” has a silent “b”.
intermediate.evidence: which is why German still says the “k” in its word for knee, Knie
intermediate.why: 第二段：德文保留了英文已消失的 k 音，證明它曾經發音。
traps: 捏造：文中沒評論德文拼字。
過度推論：文中只是拿同源字做證據。
捏造：knee 沒有 b。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe the life of William Caxton in detail.
To argue that English spelling should be reformed immediately.
To trace English spelling’s irregularities to identifiable historical causes.
To prove that all silent letters were printing errors.
advanced.evidence: Its irregularities are largely the residue of identifiable historical processes
advanced.why: 第一段點題，後面三段分別說明三個原因。
traps: 以偏概全：Caxton 只是第三段的人物。
正反顛倒：作者說改革大多失敗，重點是理解。
以偏概全：有些是學者刻意加的。

advanced.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “mistaken etymologies” in the fourth paragraph?
options: Wrong ideas about where a word came from.
Errors made by the early printers in England.
Spellings with letters that were never pronounced.
Words borrowed from merchants who spoke French.
advanced.evidence: the “s” in “island” was meant to link the word to Latin insula, whereas its true origin is the Old English īġland
advanced.why: 冒號後的例子：以為 island 來自拉丁文，其實來自古英語。
traps: 張冠李戴：印刷錯誤是第三段的原因。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：不發音是結果，不是「錯誤字源」的意思。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：商人是 Caxton 的故事。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Spelling began to be standardised after 1700.
Caxton believed English was perfectly stable in his time.
The “p” in “receipt” has always been pronounced.
The Kentish woman said she spoke no French when asked for “egges”.
advanced.evidence: was told she spoke no French, because in her dialect the word was “eyren”
traps: 時序錯置：15、16 世紀就開始標準化了。
正反顛倒：他深知語言不穩定。
正反顛倒：原文 though never pronounced。

advanced.q: What can be inferred about why spelling and pronunciation drifted apart?
options: Printers refused to print any new words.
Spelling was being fixed just as pronunciation was changing.
People stopped speaking English for two centuries.
Scholars wanted English to sound like German.
advanced.evidence: written forms were increasingly fixed just as spoken forms were shifting
advanced.why: 第二段：書寫固定下來的時候，發音正在改變。
traps: 捏造：印刷反而加速固定拼法。
捏造：文中沒有。這種說法完全不合史實。
張冠李戴：學者想讓英文看起來像拉丁文。

reflections: Choose one English word whose spelling you find strange. Look up its history in a dictionary. What story does it tell?
Should English spelling be reformed to match pronunciation? What would we gain, and what would we lose?

Reformers have tried for centuries to make the system regular, mostly without success. Yet the system is less random than it first appears. Its oddities are largely the traces of history: sound changes that spelling never caught up with, the habits of early printers, and the wishes of scholars who wanted English to look more classical.
英文拼字向來以混亂聞名。光是 ough 這幾個字母，在 tough、though、through、cough 裡的發音就各不相同，連受過教育的母語人士都會被難倒。幾百年來，改革者一直想讓它變得規則，大多沒有成功。然而這套系統並不像乍看那麼隨機。它的怪異之處，大多是歷史留下的痕跡：拼字沒跟上的發音變化、早期印刷工人的習慣，以及想讓英文看起來更古典的學者的意圖。

The most important of these changes is the Great Vowel Shift, a series of changes in pronunciation that took place mainly between 1400 and 1700. During this period, every long vowel of English altered; the vowel in “bite”, for instance, once sounded closer to the one in modern “beat”. It was just as spelling was beginning to settle down that speech was shifting, so the written forms froze while the spoken ones moved on. Consonants changed too: the “k” in “knight” and “knot” was once pronounced, as it still is in the German word for knee, Knie.
這些變化中最重要的，是「母音大推移」——主要發生在 1400 到 1700 年間的一連串發音變化。在這段期間，英文的每一個長母音都改變了；例如 bite 的母音，從前聽起來比較接近現代的 beat。正當拼字開始固定下來時，口語卻在改變，於是書寫形式凍結了，口語卻繼續往前走。子音也變了：knight 和 knot 裡的 k 曾經會發音，就像德文的「膝蓋」Knie 至今仍會發出 k 的音。

Technology added another layer. William Caxton, who is thought to have brought the printing press to England in 1476, helped fix spellings in place. Some early compositors (the workers who set the type) spoke several languages and occasionally borrowed patterns from them; the Middle English “gost”, for example, gained its silent “h” from a Flemish spelling that happened to stick. Caxton himself was well aware of how unstable English was, recalling a merchant who asked a woman for “egges” and was told she spoke no French, because in her dialect the word was “eyren”.

科技又加了一層。被認為在 1476 年把印刷機引進英國的卡克斯頓，幫助把拼字固定了下來。一些早期的排字工人（負責排列鉛字的工人）會說好幾種語言，偶爾會借用其他語言的拼法；例如中古英語的 gost，就是從一個剛好被沿用下來的法蘭德斯拼法，得到了不發音的 h。卡克斯頓自己也很清楚英語有多不穩定，他記下一個商人向一位婦人要 egges（蛋），對方卻說她不會講法語，因為在她的方言裡，這個字是 eyren。

A final layer was added on purpose. Scholars in the Renaissance and after sometimes inserted silent letters to show a word’s classical roots. The “b” in “debt” (earlier “dette”) and the “p” in “receipt” were added to make the words look Latin, though they were never pronounced. Some insertions were simply mistakes. So confident were some scholars that they added an “s” to “island” to link it with Latin insula, whereas the word actually comes from Old English.
最後一層是刻意加上的。文藝復興時期及之後的學者，有時會插入不發音的字母，來顯示一個字的古典來源。debt（早期拼作 dette）裡的 b、receipt 裡的 p，都是為了讓字看起來像拉丁文而加上的，雖然從來不發音。有些添加根本是錯的。有些學者自信到在 island 裡加了一個 s，好讓它和拉丁文 insula 連在一起，但這個字其實來自古英語。

For learners, this history offers more than trivia. Treating spelling as a record of history rather than a list of exceptions can make it easier to master. Noticing that “knee” and “knight” share a lost sound, or that “debt” is related to “debit”, turns random memorising into a meaningful pattern. Spelling, in the end, is a map of where the language has been.
對學習者來說，這段歷史不只是冷知識。把拼字當成歷史紀錄，而不是一串例外，能讓它更容易掌握。注意到 knee 和 knight 共有一個消失的音，或 debt 和 debit 有關，就能把死記硬背變成有意義的規律。說到底，拼字是一張地圖，記錄著這個語言走過的路。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why English spelling should be reformed right away.
How history explains the oddities of English spelling.
How William Caxton invented the printing press.
Why German is easier to spell than English.
questions.evidence: Its oddities are largely the traces of history
questions.why: 第一段點題，後面三段分別說明三層原因。
traps: 正反顛倒：作者說改革大多失敗，重點在理解歷史。
張冠李戴：他是把印刷機引進英國，不是發明。
捏造：德文只是用來證明 k 曾經發音。

questions.q: What does “compositors” in the third paragraph refer to?
options: Merchants who travelled to Flanders.
Scholars who studied Latin words.
Writers who composed poems in English.
Workers who set the type for printing.
questions.evidence: the workers who set the type
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：法蘭德斯只是拼法的來源。
張冠李戴：學者是第四段的人。
字面誤讀：compose 也有作曲、寫作之意，但這裡是排版。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The “k” in “knight” was once pronounced.
The Great Vowel Shift happened after 1900.
The “b” in “debt” has always been pronounced.
“Island” comes from the Latin word insula.
questions.evidence: the “k” in “knight” and “knot” was once pronounced
traps: 數字錯位：主要在 1400 到 1700 年。
正反顛倒：原文 they were never pronounced。
正反顛倒：它其實來自古英語，s 是誤加的。

questions.q: Why does the author mention the merchant who asked for “egges”?
options: To prove that English is a dialect of French.
To explain how eggs were sold in medieval markets.
To show how unstable English was in Caxton’s time.
To show that Caxton could not speak French.
questions.evidence: Caxton himself was well aware of how unstable English was
questions.why: 作者手法：用卡克斯頓記下的故事，說明當時英語有多不統一。
traps: 過度推論：婦人只是把方言字誤會成法語。
字面誤讀：重點在方言差異，不是賣蛋。
捏造：文中沒說卡克斯頓的語言能力。

mixed.prompt: Many silent letters were [47] by scholars to make words look Latin, and treating spelling as a record of history can make it easier to [48].
mixed.why: 第一格出自第四段 were added（被動）；第二格出自第五段 easier to master（to 後接原形）。

mixed.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage? Choose ALL that apply.
options: The vowel in “bite” once sounded like the one in “beat”.
Caxton is thought to have brought printing to England in 1476.
“Gost” gained its silent “h” from a Latin spelling.
The “p” in “receipt” was added to make it look Latin.
Reformers have easily made English spelling regular.
German no longer pronounces the “k” in Knie.
mixed.why: A 第二段；B 第三段；D 第四段。C 張冠李戴（來自法蘭德斯拼法）；E 正反顛倒（大多沒有成功）；F 正反顛倒（德文仍發 k 音）。
